s: We all deal with conflict and the harm that often comes with it -- with our spouses, our parents, our friends.
我们都应对冲突和经常带来的伤害 - - 我们的配偶，父母，朋友。
More than a third of Americans say that they've gone "no contact" with a friend or family member in the past year.
在过去一年中，超过三分之一的美国人表示，
And that figure rises to 60 percent among Gen Z. We live in a culture that promotes disposability, from swiping left to cancel culture.
我们生活在一个文化中，促进可处置性，从左转到取消文化。
We think we can just move on.
我们认为我们可以继续前进。
But moving on without repair can leave something behind: shame.
但如果没有修复，就会留下一些东西：耻辱。
And shame keeps that cycle of harm spinning.
羞耻让伤害的循环不断旋转。
For me, this came to light seven years ago when I started an organization with an old friend from college.
七年前，我和大学的一位老朋友创办了一个组织。
I was excited to be an entrepreneur and so invested in our work.
我很高兴成为一个企业家，所以我们投资了我们的工作。
But less than a year in to going full-time, Garrett and I were having so many issues that he decided to leave.
但在不到一年的时间里，我和加雷特有很多问题，他决定离开。
Now breakups of any kind are terrible, but this one was particularly bad because our organization was focused on racial repair.
现在任何类型的分手都很可怕，但这一次特别糟糕，因为我们的组织专注于种族纠正。
And here we were, a Black biracial woman and a white man, and we couldn't even do that repair ourselves.
在这里，我们是一位黑人女性和一个白人，我们甚至无法自己修复。
I had worked in racial justice for years and built my identity on being good at it.
我在种族司法方面工作了多年，建立我的身份是因为我擅长它。
So when Garrett left, I felt like a failure, and I was consumed with shame that then caused more issues.
所以当Garrett离开的时候，我觉得自己是一个失败者，我被羞耻吞了，然后导致了更多的问题。
I was afraid to raise hard but necessary conversations with my team.
我害怕与我的团队进行艰难但必要的对话。
I was timid in external meetings, afraid to build relationships with my peers because deep down I thought there was something wrong with me.
在外面的会议上，我很害羞，我害怕与同龄人建立关系，因为我深深地以为我有点错了。
I set standards of perfection that were impossible to meet.
我设定了无法达到的完美标准。
And then that just caused more shame.
然后，这只是造成了更多的耻辱。
And I constantly questioned my judgment.
我一直怀疑自己的判断力。
At my lowest low, I questioned my entire worth on this Earth.
在我最低的水平上，我质疑了我在地球上的全部价值。
It took me and Garrett a year and a half to come back to each other and to begin a repair process.
我和加雷特花了一年时间，一半是为了彼此相处，并开始修复过程。
But when we did, it transformed us.
但当我们这样做时，它改变了我们。
And I'm persuaded that America needs that transformation, too.
我相信美国也需要这种转型。
Because right now, we are consumed with shame.
因为现在，我们被羞耻吞了。
No matter your racial identity, most of us have felt some kind of shame about race in America.
无论您的种族身份如何，我们大多数人都对美国的种族感到羞愧。
For people of color, it's feeling less than or like we don't belong in a system that actually wasn't built for us.
对于黑色人来说，我们觉得我们不属于一个不为我们而构建的系统。
Or for white folks, it's not wanting to feel like the bad guy.
对于白人来说，这不是想感觉自己是个坏人。
You might be thinking, “I don’t feel shame.”
你可能会想，我不感到羞愧。
Or you might be thinking, “They definitely don’t feel shame.”
或许你在想，他们绝对不感到羞愧。
But psychologists agree that shame doesn't need to be conscious to be operating.
但心理学家们认为，羞耻不需要有意识才能发挥作用。
It still impacts how we act, what we avoid and who we become.
它仍然影响我们的行为，我们避免的行为以及我们成为的人。
This collective shame that we're holding is in large part because we've never repaired the harms of slavery.
我们所承担的共同耻辱主要是因为我们从来没有修复过奴隶制的伤害。
We've never fully confronted the shame of it.
我们从来没有完全面对它的耻辱。

It shouldn't be controversial to talk about slavery, or to teach the history in schools, or to acknowledge that when enslaved people were freed, they were freed into systems that were designed to keep them from ever catching up.
谈论奴隶制不应该有争议，或在学校教授历史，或承认当奴隶被释放时，他们被释放到系统中，旨在阻止他们赶上。
Compound interest [is] just one of them.
复合利息只是其中一个。
Instead, we deny the way that slavery's tentacles still impact society today.
我们否认奴隶制仍然影响社会。
Most people think that the Black-white wealth gap is closing, but it's not.
大多数人认为黑人和白人的财富差距正在缩小，
It's widening.
它正在扩大。
This is just one picture of what unrepaired structural harm looks like.
这只是一个未修复的结构损害的图像。
To heal these wounds, we need repair, also known as comprehensive reparations.
为了治愈这些伤口，我们需要修复，也称为全面补偿。
That's what the word means, by the way, from the Latin root reparare, “to repair.”
这就是这个词的意思，顺便说一下，从拉丁语的根 Reparare,
Most people think that reparations are just about money.
大多数人认为补偿只是关于钱。
But the United Nations' official definition has always gone far beyond the financial.
但联合国的官方定义始终远远超出了金融界。
Reparations are about holistic repair, making amends in structural, symbolic and material ways.
修复是整体修复，以结构性，象征性和物质的方式修复。
This is what inspired me and Garrett to cofound Liberation Ventures in the first place, to accelerate the reparations movement.
这让我和加雷特共同创立解放企业，为了加快补偿行动。
There are dozens of cities and states doing this work across the country.
全国有数十个城市和州开展这项工作。
It's happening, y'all.
这是发生的，你们所有人。
Sometimes people say to me, "Slavery was so long ago."
有时人们会对我说"，奴隶制是很久以前的。
Or, “My family didn’t own slaves.”
我家没有奴隶。
I like to invoke writer Isabel Wilkerson.
我喜欢呼唤作家伊莎贝尔·威尔克森。
She said America is like an old house with a crumbling foundation.
她说，美国就像一个老房子，
We may not have built the house, but if we want to continue living in it, it's our job to fix it.
我们也许没有建造这所房子，但如果我们愿意继续活在其中，我们的任务是修复它。
So how do we fix it?
那么我们怎么解决呢？
Fixing it starts with building a culture of repair, a culture where repair is commonsense and commonplace, and everyone has the skill and will to repair harm anytime it's caused.
修复它始于建立一个修复文化，一个修复是常识和普通话的文化，每个人都有能力和意志修复任何造成的伤害。
Now I used to be a management consultant, for better or worse, and there, they teach you to break down big challenges into their component parts.
我曾经是管理顾问，无论好还是坏，在那里，他们教你将大挑战分解成组件。
So we dug into the research and came to define repair as four components in an iterative cycle: reckoning, acknowledgment, accountability and redress.
因此，我们深入研究，并将修复定义为一个反复循环的四个组成部分：计算，承认，问责和补偿。
These four steps have been used in countries all over the world to transition out of harmful periods, often authoritarian ones, and into democracy.
这些四个步骤在世界各地已经被用来从危险时期，通常是独裁时期，转向民主时期。
And their underlying logic works on a small scale, too.
它们的基本逻辑也在小规模上运行。
So me and Garrett used this framework, and you can use it to repair in your lives, too.
所以我和加雷特使用了这个框架，你们也可以用它来修复自己的生活。
You can start at any point on the cycle, but I'll start with reckoning, which means learning.
你可以从周期的任何时候开始，但我会从计算开始，这意味着学习。
Really understanding the full truth of how harm was caused.
我真的明白了造成伤害的全部真相。
Garrett and I sat down with a facilitator and shared the details of our experiences with each other.
我和加雷特和一个助手坐下来，互相分享了我们的经历。
And let me tell you, when I started, I had so much going on in my body, I could barely speak words.
让我告诉你，当我开始时，我的身体发生了很多事情，我几乎不能说话。
But we kept trying until we had a shared understanding of what went wrong.
但我们一直在努力，直到我们共同理解错误了什么。
At the societal level, over 50 countries have gone through at-scale reckoning processes.
在社会层面上，有50多个国家经历了大规模的计算过程。
The most famous is South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which spent seven years documenting the harms of apartheid.
最著名的是南非的真理和和解委员会，七年时间记录种族隔离的危害。
They held 2,500 public hearings, took 21,000 statements from victims -- 2,000 of those people read their stories aloud.
他们举行了2500次公开听证会，接受了21000名受害者的陈述，其中2000人大声阅读他们的故事。
This level of truth-telling has no American equivalent -- at least not yet.
这种讲真相水平没有美国的同等，至少还没有。
The next is acknowledgment, which means naming and voicing that harm in public -- saying, “Yes, this happened.”
接下来是承认，这意味着在公共场合命名和表达这种伤害-- 说"，是的，这发生了
Garrett and I spent hours reflecting each other's stories back to each other, so that we both felt seen and heard.
我和加雷特花了几个小时反思彼此的故事，让我们都觉得自己被看见和被听到。
At the societal level, we can look to postwar Germany and how they healed after the atrocities of the Holocaust.
在社会层面上，我们可以看看战后的德国，
Germany built acknowledgment into physical space at extraordinary scale.
德国在非凡的规模上建立了对物理空间的认可。
They built around 300 memorial sites, and 70,000 small brass plaques were installed in front of the last known addresses of Holocaust victims.
他们建造了大约300个纪念碑，和7万个小铜牌安装在Holocaust受害者最后一个已知地址前。
In Germany, Holocaust education is required in every school.
在德国，每个学校都需要接受大屠杀教育。
Next, accountability, which means taking ownership and committing to change.
接下来是问责制，这意味着承担责任，
I took what I learned from the process I went through with Garrett and put practices in place at Liberation Ventures to help ensure that that kind of conflict and harm never happens again.
我从加雷特的过程中学到的东西，在"解放企业" (Liberation Ventures) 中，伤害永远不会再发生。
And at the macro level, we can look to Colombia.
在宏观层面上，我们可以看看哥伦比亚。
After 52 years of conflict, five million people displaced, 200,000 people killed, the Colombian government took accountability for healing.
在52年的冲突之后，500万人流离失所，哥伦比亚政府对治愈负责。
They passed a victims law, which was designed to repair not only physical harm but also psychological trauma.
他们通过了一项受害者法，为了修复不仅身体伤害，而且心理创伤。
And then two years later, they passed a universal mental health care law for everyone, not just victims.
两年后，他们通过了一项普遍的精神医疗保健法，
Finally, redress: acts of restitution, financial compensation, returning what was taken, healing the wound.
最后，补偿：归还行为，经济补偿，返回被夺走的东西，治愈伤口。
For me and Garrett, this mostly looks like finding small ways to help each other in each of our respective endeavors.
对于我和加雷特来说，这主要看起来像在我们各自的努力中找到帮助彼此的小方法。
He helped me with this talk.
他帮我讲这个话。
And at the societal level, we can look right here at home.
在社会层面上，我们可以在家中看看。
In 1988, President Reagan signed the Civil Liberties Act, which acknowledged that the federal government had forcibly incarcerated 120,000 Japanese Americans without due process.
1988年，里根总统签署了公民自由法案，该法案承认联邦政府在没有正当程序的情况下强制监禁了120,000名日本裔美国人。
Twenty thousand dollars was paid to each survivor, totaling approximately $1.6 billion.
每个幸存者都得到了20万美元，总额约为16亿美元。
And that program was implemented over multiple presidential administrations from both parties.
两党的多个总统政府实施了这一计划。
And by the way, Germany has also made ongoing payments to Holocaust survivors and descendants of victims.
德国还向大屠杀幸存者和受害者的后代进行了持续支付。
They’ve paid almost 100 billion euros over time.
随着时间的推移，他们已经支付了近1亿欧元。
Reckoning, acknowledgment, accountability and redress.
清算，承认，问责和补偿。
Repair requires all four because together, they make each other real.
修复需要四个，因为一起，它们使彼此成为现实。
Each of these stories is an example of a country choosing to move through shame and toward repair.
每个故事都是一个国家选择克服羞耻，
And none of them are perfect.
没有一个完美。
All of them are unfinished, and some of them have been intentionally tested, eroded or undone.
所有这些都是未完成的，有些是故意被测试，被侵蚀或废除的。
But we can't do nothing just because we can't do everything.
但我们不能做任何事情，因为我们不能做一切。
If all of these countries can do it, so can we.
如果所有这些国家都能做到这一点，我们也可以。
Building a culture of repair starts with each of us, in our own lives.
修复的文化始于我们每个人的生活中。
A few years ago,
几年前，
I was at home for the Christmas holidays in Colorado, and I was sitting on the couch across from my mom when she looked up from her phone and asked me, "Are you ashamed of me because I'm white?"
我在科罗拉多度过圣诞节，我坐在我母亲对面的沙发上，她从手机上抬头问我，"你因为我是白人而感到羞愧吗？"
I knew why she was asking, but I pretended not to.
我知道为什么她问，但我假装没有。
I denied it because I didn't want to face it.
我拒绝了，因为我不想面对它。
But she had been looking at photos that I had posted on social media of my family over the holidays, and I hadn't posted a single one of her.
但她一直在看我在社交媒体上发布的照片，我还没有发布她的任何照片。
And when I got back to my apartment in Brooklyn a couple days later, I realized I don't have any pictures of her on my wall either.
几天后，当我回到布鲁克林的公寓时，我意识到我在墙上也没有她的照片。
My shame about my mom’s whiteness -- and therefore the whiteness in me -- is not about my mom.
我对我的白色感到羞愧 - - 因此我内心的白色 - - 不是因为我。
It’s shame about where the story of American slavery stalls, with harm to millions of people across centuries.
美国奴隶制的故事在哪里？，几百年来对数百万人造成了伤害。
I started working through this shame, through acknowledgment.
我开始克服这种羞耻，通过承认。
I stopped hiding my whiteness, and I started telling that story publicly.
我不再隐藏我的白色，我开始公开讲述这个故事。
Very publicly, today.
今天非常公开。
And over time, I started to feel more whole.
随着时间的推移，我开始感觉更完整。
I was claiming my whole biracial self and [was]clear that my whole self belongs.
我宣称自己是个种族主义者，我明白自己是个民族。
And I realized, that's the same journey that this nation needs.
我意识到，这是这个国家需要的旅程。
Because repair doesn't just fix what's broken.
因为修复不仅仅是修复坏的东西。
Repair transforms us.
修复改变了我们。
It transformed me and Garrett, it transformed Colombia and Germany and South Africa, and it can transform America, too.
它改变了我和加雷特，它改变了哥伦比亚，德国，南非，它也可以改变美国。
Imagine the genuine pride that we would feel if repair was the last chapter in this story.
想象一下，如果修复是这篇故事的最后章节，我们会感到真正的骄傲。
For 250 years, the shame of slavery has haunted us.
250年来，奴隶制的耻辱一直困扰着我们。
It has corroded our democracy.
它破坏了我们的民主。
Building a culture of repair is the only path that will change that.
修复文化是唯一改变这一点的道路。
It's the only path that gets us to our highest national ideal.
这是唯一的道路，使我们达到最高的国家理想。
One nation, indivisible.
一个国家，不可分割。
Thank you.
谢谢你。
